question.text: The 'Fit and Proper' test under SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations 2008 evaluates:

answer.text: Integrity, honesty, ethical behaviour, reputation, fairness, character, and absence of SEBI-specified disqualifications of the applicant and its key personnel
Only the financial net worth of the applicant entity
Whether the applicant has passed the relevant NISM certification exam
The applicant's years of experience in the securities market exclusively

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.55, the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations 2008 fit-and-proper test is based on integrity, honesty, ethical behaviour, reputation, fairness, character, and the absence of SEBI-specified disqualifications, assessed for the entity and its key personnel. The Trap: Fit and proper is not limited to financial net worth, NISM certification, or years of experience. Capital adequacy, experience, and infrastructure are separate RTA registration criteria covered on workbook pp.69 and 72, not part of the fit-and-proper test itself. Note: Keep the fit-and-proper criteria (integrity, honesty, ethics, reputation, fairness, character, disqualifications) separate from the broader registration eligibility tests for RTAs.
